subject: QBR playbook + escalation matrix — cross-functional prep and sign-off
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Kate Miller <kate@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: QBR playbook + escalation matrix — cross-functional prep and sign-off

Team —

Thanks for jumping on this thread. With the ACME QBR scheduled for Nov 12, I want to get a tight cross-functional checkpoint in place for playbook sign-off and the escalation matrix. Attached is the latest draft of the QBR playbook (QBR_playbook_v2.pdf) and an escalation matrix sketch that I pulled from the last run (escalation_matrix_v3.xlsx).

High level asks:
- Review the playbook sections that map to your area (GTM, pricing, docs, support). I flagged pages: 7 (pricing cadence), 12–14 (enablement delivery), 18–22 (support SLAs + SLOs).
- Confirm the escalation owners and on-call rotation in the matrix by EOD Monday (Nov 9).
- Kim, can docs confirm where the customer-facing runbook will live? Marcus, can Support validate the runbook steps and triage flow?

Kate — I’ve copied you so ACME has visibility into our timeline. If there are ACME-specific items you want surfaced in the QBR, flag them here; we’ll fold them into the playbook.

I’m proposing a 30-min triage on Mon (Nov 9) at 10am PT to resolve remaining owners and close open items. Please confirm availability.

Thanks — Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, GTM Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR playbook + escalation matrix — cross-functional prep and sign-off

Thanks Vivek — quick pricing question: the playbook references promotional credits for ACME in the renewal slide (page 7). Is that already approved by finance/sales ops or is that something we need to escalate for leadership sign-off? If it’s not approved, I want to make sure the QBR narrative doesn’t promise it.

Also: I’ll be at the Monday 10am sync.

Ben
Senior Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR playbook + escalation matrix — cross-functional prep and sign-off

Looping in enablement notes: I reviewed pages 12–14 and added a short enablement agenda for the QBR that includes product highlights, 2 customer stories (we should surface the ACME PoC outcome), and a hands-on demo of the latency/cost dashboards. I’ve uploaded a short presenter checklist into the playbook (see section header).

Open item for Product/Docs: we need one two-pager for ACME that summarizes rollout timeline + known limits (token ceilings, latency SLOs) — Kim, can you confirm a delivery date for that? Ideally we have the two-pager by Nov 10 for prep.

Marissa
Director, Customer Enablement | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR playbook + escalation matrix — cross-functional prep and sign-off

Support notes: I reviewed the support runbook and added inline comments to support_runbook_draft.md (see attachment). Key asks:
- Confirm error categories that map to immediate escalation (P0/P1) vs. next-day (P2) — I flagged three scenarios where automatic fallback to a cheaper model should be explicitly documented.
- We need a recovery play (page 20) that covers data exfiltration, audit logs request process, and how we spin up a Dedicated pool for customers with predictable throughput issues.

I’ll join Monday 10am but if we need a separate ops-runbook deep dive I can schedule a 60-min run-through with SRE.

Marcus
Senior Manager, Support | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR playbook + escalation matrix — cross-functional prep and sign-off

Attached: support_runbook_draft.md (updated), and an updated doc hosting plan.

Quick answers:
- Two-pager for ACME: I can have a first pass by EOD Nov 9 and final by Nov 10.
- Doc hosting: customer-facing runbook will live in the customer docs site (docs.redwood.ai/acme) with a private preview link we can share in the QBR. I added the preview link into the playbook (Notion link).
- Escalation owners: I confirmed primary/secondary owners in the matrix; see escalation_matrix_v3.xlsx. Please review owner initials and flag any conflicts — I assigned Marcus as primary for P0 technical incidents and Ben as primary for commercial escalations.

Kimberly
Head of Docs & Developer Evangelism | Redwood Inference
From: Kate Miller <kate@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR playbook + escalation matrix — cross-functional prep and sign-off

Thanks everyone — this looks comprehensive. A couple of ACME asks before the Nov 12 QBR: 
1) We would like a short rehearsal on Nov 11 (30 min) focused on the demo and the two-pager messaging. Will that work?
2) Can Redwood provide a pre-prod sandbox and temporary credentials so our SRE can validate the failover path you mention (automatic fallback to cheaper model)?
3) On pricing: we appreciate the note about promotional credits. Please confirm if that is still pending internal approval — we don’t want to take that as a commitment during the QBR.

Kate Miller
Director of Cloud Engineering | Acme Enterprises
